note: Pre-rendered branded topic cards (no figures, so they never go stale). Used when a dynamic image cannot be hosted. Facts and sources always go in the post text.

inflation: When prices rise faster than incomes, the same money buys less.
interest-rates: Rate decisions affect mortgages, savings and the cost of borrowing.
jobs-wages: Employment and pay growth shape household budgets.
growth: How fast the economy grows affects jobs, incomes and government budgets.
housing: Housing costs are one of the largest parts of most household budgets.
energy: Fuel and power prices flow through to transport, food and bills.
currency: Exchange rates change what money is worth across borders.
trade: Developments overseas can reach household costs at home.
budget-tax: Government decisions change what households pay and receive.
cost-of-living: Understanding where money goes is the first step in planning.
retirement: Long-term planning starts with understanding today's choices.
education-costs: Planning early helps families prepare for rising costs.
resilience: Emergency savings and planning help households absorb shocks.
explainer: Understanding the terms is the first step to better decisions.
